prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures a laboratory scene where the camera wearer starts facing a cluttered workbench (0.5 to 1.0 m away, within arm's reach, with a gloved hand briefly appearing at <0.4 m in frame 1) and turns rightward across frames 1 to 5 toward an open corridor (>4 m deep, dark black) bounded by a central grey partition wall (1.5 to 3.5 m away). On the benchtop, a centrifuge on the left, a central black ice bucket, stacked petri dishes, tip boxes, and reagent bottles on both the counter and upper shelf sit 0.2 to 0.5 m apart, while in frames 4 and 5 a person carrying a red container at waist level (within their own arm's reach) enters from the right edge at ~2.5 to 3.0 m and walks forward to ~2.0 to 2.5 m in front of the camera wearer, ~1 m right of the wall corner and in front of a distant bench (3 to 4 m). Compared to RGB alone, the depth map more clearly reveals the continuous recession of the uniform grey partition wall and floor, the sharp depth discontinuity between the near bench corner (<0.6 m, bright white) and the corridor behind it, and the 3D layering of overlapping bottles and boxes on the counter. However, the map is unreliable in maintaining consistent depth scaling across frames (saturating the left bench corner to pure white in frames 4 and 5 once the deep hallway enters view), merges transparent glass bottles on the upper shelf into the background, and flattens the approaching person into a uniform grey silhouette that obscures that they are facing and looking toward the camera wearer with their right hand raised.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates selected small containers on the workbench and upper shelf in frames 1 to 4 (at 0.5 to 1.2 m, mostly within the camera wearer's arm's reach and 0.1 to 0.5 m from each other) and tracks the approaching person on the right in frames 4 and 5 as the camera wearer turns right away from the bench. In frame 4, the person mask is partially occluded and cropped by the right frame edge at ~2.5 to 3.0 m, and in frame 5 the full silhouette stands at ~2.0 to 2.5 m on the right, flanked by two adjacent masks labeled 'suitcase' representing the red container held in their left hand (within their arm's reach) and a white lab coat hanging on a bench ~1 m behind them. Compared to the RGB strip, the colored masks provide crisp pixel-level boundaries that separate overlapping reagent bottles on the counter and cleanly segment the approaching person's full contour from the bright hallway floor and background clutter. However, the map is highly unreliable in class labeling and recall: it misses the vast majority of the scene (the bench, upper shelves, centrifuge, fire extinguisher, and the camera wearer's hand in frame 1), misclassifies labware into out-of-domain COCO labels ('mouse' for a chair edge, 'bowl' for the ice bucket, 'cup' for stacked petri dishes, 'book' for boxes, 'tv' for wall signs, and 'suitcase' for the held red bin and hanging coat), and provides no internal body structure to tell which way the person is facing or looking.
descriptions.pose: Across the 5 frames as the camera wearer turns right from the workbench (0.5 to 1.0 m away, within arm's reach) toward the corridor on the right (2 to 4 m away), the pose map is almost entirely empty black space except for a single yellow skeleton rendered in the lower-center-right of frame 4. Using the RGB strip for context, a blue-gloved hand of the camera wearer appears at the bottom center of frame 1 (<0.4 m), and a person in a white lab coat enters on the far right of frame 4 (~2.5 to 3.0 m, mostly cropped) before stepping into full view in frame 5 (~2.0 to 2.5 m away on the right), facing and looking directly toward the camera wearer while holding a red container in their left hand and raising their right gloved hand to chest height (both hands within their own arm's reach and ~0.3 m apart). The pose map adds no valid spatial information beyond RGB because it completely fails to detect any real human bodies or hands in the sequence. Instead, it is wholly unreliable, omitting both the camera wearer's near hand in frame 1 and the approaching person with clearly visible body and hand joints in frames 4 and 5, while hallucinating a small, horizontally oriented yellow body skeleton onto inanimate reagent bottles and petri dishes on the right corner of the lab bench (~0.6 to 0.8 m away) in frame 4.
